images.title: Twelfths make adding easy
images.purpose: Show 1/6 and 1/4 both rewritten as twelfths, because 12 is the LCM of 6 and 4, and then added.
images.composition: Three equal fraction bars stacked in the centre, one caption line at the top and short labels at the right, generous white space.
exact_structure: Every bar is the same length and is split by thin grey #6B7280 lines into exactly 12 equal cells.
Bar 1: the first 2 cells filled teal #0072B2, a thicker teal line after cell 2, other 10 cells white. Label at right: 1/6 = 2/12.
Bar 2: the first 3 cells filled amber #E69F00, a thicker amber line after cell 3, other 9 cells white. Label at right: 1/4 = 3/12.
Bar 3: 2 teal cells then 3 amber cells, 5 filled in all, other 7 cells white, outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7. Label at right: 2/12 + 3/12 = 5/12.
rejection: any bar with a count of cells other than 12
images.takeaway: Using the LCM of the denominators as the common denominator keeps the numbers small.
images.description: Three 12 cell bars: 2 teal cells for 1/6, 3 amber cells for 1/4, and 5 cells for the sum 5/12.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on adding fractions with the LCM.
images.teaching_notes: Count the cells in each bar; all three are cut into twelfths, so the shaded cells simply add.

image_decisions.why: Fraction bars show why the LCM works as the common denominator.
